;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Attack on the United States embassy in Baghdad]]
**Supporters of [[Iraq]]i [[paramilitaries]] withdraw from the [[Embassy of the United States, Baghdad|American embassy in Baghdad]] after being ordered to by the [[Popular Mobilization Forces]], stating the "message has been heard". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security-usa/iraqi-militias-start-withdrawing-from-u-s-embassy-idUSKBN1Z01N9?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]], [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] release six [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] prisoners as part of a [[United Nations]]-mediated deal struck last month. All six arrive in [[Riyadh]] later the same day. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-prisoners/six-saudi-prisoners-freed-by-yemens-houthis-return-home-idUSKBN1Z01T9?il=0 (Reuters)]
**The [[Secessionism|secessionist]] [[Southern Transitional Council]] pulls out of committees working to implement a November agreement that would have placed them in [[Cabinet of Yemen|the national cabinet]] and put their forces under government control. The council claims it was in response to an outbreak of violence in the [[Shabwah Governorate]] allegedly caused by their rival, the [[Al-Islah (Yemen)|Al-Islah]] party. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security/yemens-southern-separatists-pull-out-of-riyadh-agreement-committees-idUSKBN1Z01ZE?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Taliban]] kills 23 security force members in three separate attacks in three different [[Provinces of Afghanistan|Afghani provinces]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/taliban-attacks-kill-20-afghan-security-forces-200101133724551.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019–20 Australian bushfire season]]
**An additional three deaths have been confirmed on the [[New South Wales]] [[South Coast (New South Wales)|South Coast]] while another man has been killed in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]'s [[East Gippsland]] region. [https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-and-victorian-bushfires-wreak-havoc-and-destruction/live-coverage/fb3443775d5d2b365ba1c583046dc865 (''News'')]
*[[2020 Jakarta floods]]
**At least 21 people are killed and over 19,000 displaced as [[flash flood]]s hit the [[Indonesia]]n capital of [[Jakarta]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50969418 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Coast Guard]] searches for five missing crew members after a fishing vessel sinks near [[Kodiak, Alaska]]. Two other crew members are rescued. [https://www.ktuu.com/content/news/Coast-Guard-searching-for-5-people--566629771.html (NBC News)]
*A fire at [[Krefeld Zoo]], [[NRW]], [[Germany]], kills over 30 animals. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-50971250 (BBC News)] 

;Health and environment
*[[Palau]] becomes the first country in the world to ban [[sunscreen|sun cream]] that is harmful to corals and sea life. The ban comes into effect immediately after an announcement by [[President of Palau|President]] [[Thomas Remengesau Jr.]] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50963080 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–United States relations]], [[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] says his nation will be "developing a new strategic weapon" in the near future, after the [[United States]] misses a year-end deadline for a restart of denuclearization talks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-usa/kim-says-north-korea-to-show-new-strategic-weapon-in-near-future-idUSKBN1YZ1DX?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[China–Indonesia relations]], [[Spratly Islands dispute]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Indonesia)|Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] rejects an earlier statement by [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] spokesman [[Geng Shuang]] that [[China]] had territorial claims to the [[Spratly Islands]] as part of the [[Nine-Dash Line]], stating it "[has] no legal basis and have never been recognized by the [[United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea|UNCLOS 1982]]". Indonesia had recalled its ambassador to China two days earlier after a [[China Coast Guard|Chinese coastguard]] vessel trespassed in its waters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indonesia-china-southchinasea/indonesia-rejects-chinas-claims-over-south-china-sea-idUSKBN1Z01RE?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*At least 16 inmates are killed and five others injured in a riot that breaks out at a prison in [[Zacatecas]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-50965785 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Guinea-Bissau presidential election]]
**Former [[Prime Minister of Guinea-Bissau]] [[Umaro Sissoco Embaló]] is declared the winner of the country's presidential elections. However, his direct rival [[Domingos Simões Pereira]] says he will challenge the results in court. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bissau-election/ex-guinea-bissau-pm-embalo-wins-presidency-opponent-disputes-vote-idUSKBN1Z01RA (Reuters)]
*[[Investigations involving Benjamin Netanyahu]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] announces he will seek [[Legal immunity|immunity]] from his corruption cases. As the [[Knesset]] is currently deadlocked, they will likely not come to a decision until after [[2020 Israeli legislative election|the next election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-politics-netanyahu/israels-netanyahu-says-he-will-seek-immunity-in-graft-cases-idUSKBN1Z020L?il=0 (Reuters)]  
*[[Politics of Switzerland]]
**[[Simonetta Sommaruga]] is sworn in as [[President of the Swiss Confederation]] for second time. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/europe/2020-01/01/c_138671825.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
*[[Politics of Austria]]
**[[Austria]]'s left-wing [[The Greens – The Green Alternative|Green Party]] agrees to form a coalition with the ruling right-wing [[Austrian People's Party|People's Party]]. This will be the first time the Green Party is part of a ruling government in the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-50969001 (BBC News)]
